<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b><i>~*~ Welcome to my island! ~*~</i></b><br>
  <b>Castaway</b> is a ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.<br>
  One young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. She mostly nods to the music on her headphones.
  Every so often, on the beat, something happens. Then she goes back to nodding.<br>
  <sub>Working title &nbsp;·&nbsp; an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i> &nbsp;·&nbsp; in development, no video yet</sub>
</p>

**What happens on my island.** Mostly nothing, and that is the product: a stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams, 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, sunny and hand-painted, and always daytime. Then she puts a note in a bottle, throws it out to sea, and it washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A shark surfaces, also in headphones, and nods to the same beat. More than 90 activities in [activities.toml](activities.toml) take turns, most of them on four timers and the rest as follow-ups, and every one of them waits for the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat.

**Everything you hear is made from code.** [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py) synthesizes all of it, more than 150 sound files including the theme and the ocean, from maths alone: no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ My gags!!! ~*~</b> the things that happen while you are not looking</summary>
<br>

Here is some of what might happen, at random, in one ten-hour video. Some of it every few minutes. Some of it once, if you are lucky. Two are marked NEW!, because a homepage has to mark something NEW!

- **The bottle.** She writes a note, corks it in a bottle and throws it out to sea. It washes straight back.
- <img src="assets/61-web-1-homepage_opus_5.5-new.svg" width="40" height="20" alt="NEW!"> **The reply.** Much later, a different bottle brings an answer.
- **The drone.** A delivery drone lowers a parcel. Inside: another pair of headphones.
- **The turtle.** A sea turtle drops by.
- <img src="assets/61-web-1-homepage_opus_5.5-new.svg" width="40" height="20" alt="NEW!"> **The cat.** A stray cat, a grey tabby with a white chest, arrives on a crate, climbs the palm and naps. One day it floats away again. Another day, the cat comes back.
- **The signal hunt.** One bar of signal, at the very top of the palm. (This page was probably uploaded from up there.)
- **The shark.** A shark in headphones surfaces and nods to the beat.
- **The tour boat.** A small boat full of people taking selfies.
- **The coconut.** A coconut falls on a hermit crab. Then the coconut walks off, with the crab wearing it.
- **She could leave any time.** Very rarely she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.
- **The hydrofoil.** A bro on an electric hydrofoil carves in, waves a shaka and carves off.
- **Bushcraft.** Fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing.
- **The kumara.** Planted once, it grows over the course of the video.
- **The regulars.** Sipping a coconut, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue, and a sandcastle that stands until the tide takes it.

The island keeps itself busy too: 26 bits of scene life, 4 always on and 22 that come and go. The shore waves and the drifting cloud shadows are built. Distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ My schedule (very important) ~*~</b> four timers, one beat</summary>
<br>

Most activities sit on one of four timers in [activities.toml](activities.toml); a dozen or so only ever follow on from another one. Counts are the median of 200 simulated ten-hour runs, as the file's own header gives them.

<table align="center">
  <tr><th>Timer</th><th>Comes round every</th><th>In a 10-hour run</th></tr>
  <tr><td>regular</td><td>2 to 5 minutes</td><td align="right">about 155</td></tr>
  <tr><td>occasional</td><td>12 to 25 minutes</td><td align="right">about 30</td></tr>
  <tr><td>rare</td><td>30 to 60 minutes</td><td align="right">about 13</td></tr>
  <tr><td>super rare</td><td>3 to 6 hours, 3 at most</td><td align="right">about 2</td></tr>
  <tr><td>chained</td><td>straight after another one</td><td align="right">about 20</td></tr>
</table>

She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Every activity starts on the next bar of the 80 BPM theme (a bar is 3 seconds), so even the rarest gag lands on the beat. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea can get on with something while she is busy with a coconut. The default run is `10:00:00` on seed `1992`, and the same seed gives the same schedule, event for event.

```sh
python tools/schedule.py      # check the schedule and simulate a 10-hour run
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ Cool sounds!!! ~*~</b> all of them made from code</summary>
<br>

[tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py) makes every sound from scratch, more than 150 files and counting, with no samples, no loops and no recordings, so nothing in the soundtrack carries a third-party licence.

- **The theme** is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major: ii, V, I, vi, 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and the ticks and hiss of an old record.
- **The ocean** is a seamless 60-second loop as well.
- **The mix** sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the levels can be set for the master and for each routine.

Nobody has listened to any of it yet, so this homepage cannot tell you whether it is good. It can tell you it is exactly 60 seconds long.

```sh
python tools/make_audio.py    # needs numpy, and ffmpeg on PATH
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ How my homepage works ~*~</b> the renderer, the export, the dev reel</summary>
<br>

The renderer is a web page. [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py) serves [web/index.html](web/index.html) with a live preview of the island and an export button. The browser encodes every frame exactly with WebCodecs (H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes in the sound and joins the two into a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules: no build step, no npm packages.

```sh
python tools/serve.py               # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py            # check the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev   # older renderer: a dev reel with a HUD
```

Hard cuts and stepped movement are the project's motion defaults, which is also how everything on this page moves, like a GIF.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ FAQ ~*~</b> frequently asked questions, asked by nobody, frequently</summary>
<br>

**Does anything happen?** Yes. Every so often. On the beat.

**How often?** Something ordinary every 2 to 5 minutes. Something rare every 30 to 60 minutes. Something super rare once or twice a video, three times at the very most.

**Why are there stars? It is always daytime.** The stars are this page's wallpaper. On the island it is always daytime, and that is a rule.

**Can she leave?** She could leave any time. Very rarely she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.

**What is the ship for?** It waits until she is busy, then sails past. She is busy with a coconut. She never sees it.

**Is this the 1992 screensaver?** No. It is an unofficial remake inspired by its small-island routines and visual comedy: a different castaway, a different island, about the same amount of waiting.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>~*~ View source ~*~</b> how this homepage was made</summary>
<br>

The look is the free personal homepage of the late 1990s, the vernacular web that Olia Lialina catalogued in her 2005 essay: a tiled starry background, a serif welcome line in a clashing colour, a 3D logo from a free logo generator, a rainbow rule, a NEW! starburst, an under-construction sign with flashing lamps, a marquee, an odometer hit counter, a webring and a drawer of 88x31 buttons. GitHub strips `<marquee>` and `<blink>`, so all the motion lives inside the pictures, and because each button is its own image, each one can be a real link.

Nothing here is copied from an archived page, GIF, button or site. A small generator script draws every pixel:

- **Four fonts, drawn by hand:** a bold Roman at 9 px caps for the welcome line, the way a browser's serif came out on an unsmoothed screen; a 7 px sans for the small print; 3x5 capitals for inside the buttons; and the counter's figures.
- **The logo** is eight letters drawn as centre-line strokes, rasterised hard-edged on an arch, extruded in deep purples and matted in black, with a rainbow that steps one band a beat.
- **The photo** is dithered like a 256-colour GIF and annotated in paint-program red.
- **Every animation cuts like a GIF** and keeps the theme's time: 0.75 seconds a beat, 3 seconds a bar. She nods on the beat, the photo's story takes 8 bars, and the lamps and the NEW! swap once a beat, far below anything that flashes. With reduced motion turned on, everything holds a complete, readable frame.

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>castaway is Away.</b> She will get back to you in two to five minutes, on the beat.<br>
  <sub>working title &middot; a 10-hour lo-fi island video for YouTube &middot; 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps &middot; always daytime<br>an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, not affiliated with it</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="tools/serve.py">Start a conversation</a> &middot;
  <a href="activities.toml">View contacts</a> &middot;
  <a href="tools/schedule.py">Check her schedule</a> &middot;
  <a href="tools/make_audio.py">Send a sound</a> &middot;
  <a href="MUSING.md">View message history</a>
</p>

One young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens: a message in a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone brings her another pair of headphones, a shark in headphones nods along, a stray cat naps up the palm. Her best signal is one bar, at the very top of that palm, which is why her status says what it says. A stationary-frame video in the spirit of the ten-hour lo-fi streams, with the small-island routines and visual comedy of a 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime scene.

**More than 90 activities** live in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml) (94 as of 2026-10-02): most on four timers, from every 2 to 5 minutes to every 3 to 6 hours, the rest chained follow-ups. Each one starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

That is the whole sign-in: a web page with a live preview of the island and an export to a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. No video has been published yet, so for now this is the only way to watch her wait.

<summary><b>Tools</b>: the other windows on her desktop</summary>

- [`python tools/serve.py`](tools/serve.py), then <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a>: the renderer ([`web/index.html`](web/index.html)). Live preview, and frame-exact export in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome); the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4.
- [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py): validates the schedule and simulates a 10-hour run.
- [`python tools/render_demo.py --dev`](tools/render_demo.py): a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display (the older Python reference renderer).
- [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): where every sound comes from.

Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, which is why she goes up and down the palm in the banner without climbing. More in [`MUSING.md`](MUSING.md).

<p align="center">
  <b>The future of doing nothing.</b><br>
  <sub>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens. On purpose, on schedule, and on the beat.</sub>

<p align="center">
  A young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back to her feet. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the coconut walks off.<br>
  <sub>A stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the 10-hour lo-fi streams, and an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime. 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps. Always daytime.</sub>

  <b>SYNTHESIZED.</b> The theme, the ocean, the gulls, the ship's horn: all made by code. No samples, no recordings.<br>
  <b>MILLENNIUM READY.</b> It is always daytime, so midnight never comes. Very little happens.

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours in which almost nothing happens. The codec is delighted.</b>
</p>

<p align="center">
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the 10-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A bro on an electric hydrofoil throws a shaka and carves off.<br>
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 screensaver. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime. 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  More than 90 activities, most of them on four timers, from everyday routines every 2 to 5 minutes to super-rare callbacks every 3 to 6 hours. Each one starts on the next bar of the music, so every gag lands on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code in <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><code>tools/make_audio.py</code></a>: no samples, no stock loops, no recordings.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then export a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm.<br>
  The browser export asks for a keyframe every 2 seconds and lets the other 59 frames in each 60 say <i>same as before</i>, give or take a wave. The banner above has lost its keyframe on purpose, so you can only tell when something moves. On this island, that takes a while.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>ERROR LOG</b>: what breaks, on which bar, and why</summary>

```text
 CASTAWAY_SEED1992_10H.MP4 · ERROR LOG · ONE LOOP = 15 S = 5 BARS
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 BAR 1   0.0 s   P-FRAME · SAME AS BEFORE
                 nothing happens. she nods on every beat (80 BPM, so
                 every 0.75 s). this is most of the video, and about
                 the cheapest kind of frame there is
 BAR 2   3.0 s   P-FRAME · SAME AS BEFORE, SIDEWAYS
                 slice displacement: bands of the frame slide sideways,
                 the title splits into red, green and blue, and one strip
                 of it stutters down the frame, twice. 340 ms, then back
 BAR 3   6.0 s   P-FRAME · SOMETHING MOVED
                 a bro on an electric hydrofoil, in stepped movement at
                 12.5 steps a second. there is no keyframe to correct
                 him, so his colours drag behind him in 8-unit blocks:
                 a datamosh. he throws a shaka. her eyes are shut
 BAR 4   9.0 s   I-FRAME · KEYFRAME. ALL BETTER
                 the keyframe lands and the smear is gone, but for 300 ms
                 the colour table is wrong: the sky acid green, the sea
                 hot pink, a band of pure magenta, a line of cyan
 BAR 5  12.0 s   P-FRAME · SORTED BY BRIGHTNESS
                 pixel sort: from a brightness threshold downwards, the
                 title, the sun, the clouds and the sand are dragged into
                 smooth comb-like streaks. 400 ms, then nothing at all
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 WHY ON THE BAR ...... every activity in Castaway starts on the next bar
                       of the music (every 3 s), so the gags land on the
                       beat. the glitches here keep the same rule
 FLASHING ............ every burst is local and short, and starts on
                       its own bar, three seconds after the last. with
                       reduced motion the banner stops on the
                       hydrofoil mid-smear, title clean
 THE BYTES ........... in a raw H.264 stream, 00 00 00 01 is the start
                       code in front of each NAL unit. a 41 after it
                       begins a slice of an ordinary frame, a 65 a
                       slice of a keyframe. the browser export hands
                       the server this kind of stream, with a keyframe
                       every 2 s. the rest of each line here is made up
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>DATABEND</b>: the gag list, with one byte changed per line</summary>

Databending means editing a file's bytes and seeing what the format makes of them. Here are some of the island's routines, each with exactly one byte changed. Offsets count from zero.

```text
 OFF  BYTE    WAS                               IS NOW
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

 18   63→74   back with an iced coffee          back with an iced toffee
 30   61→69   a coconut falls on a hermit crab  a coconut falls on a hermit crib
 10   69→61   fire by friction                  fire by fraction
 11   73→62   building a sandcastle             building a bandcastle
 07   62→67   a tour boat of selfie-takers      a tour goat of selfie-takers
 06   66→77   spear fishing                     spear wishing
 09   74→62   the tide takes it                 the tide bakes it
 00   77→72   waving for rescue                 raving for rescue
 16   65→6F   nodding to the beat               nodding to the boat
 06   79→77   a stray cat                       a straw cat
```

The video itself is not databent. Unbent, the island goes like this:

```text
 NOW SHOWING, EVERY SO OFTEN (a few of the more than 90)
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 · a message in a bottle that washes straight back to her. a different
   bottle, later, brings a reply
 · a delivery drone. the parcel is another pair of headphones
 · a sea turtle who visits
 · a grey tabby with a white chest who arrives on a crate, climbs the

 · the signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the top of the palm
 · a shark wearing headphones, nodding to the beat
 · a tour boat of selfie-takers
 · a coconut falls on a hermit crab. the coconut walks off, with the
   crab wearing it
 · she could leave any time: she walks out over the water and comes
   back with an iced coffee
 · a bro on an electric hydrofoil: a shaka, a carve, gone
 · bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear
   fishing
 · a kumara she plants, which grows over the course of the video
 · coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue
 · a sandcastle. the tide takes it
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>GOP STRUCTURE</b>: the schedule, which is also mostly same as before</summary>

In a video stream, a group of pictures is a keyframe followed by frames that only describe what changed. Castaway's day works the same way: long stretches of idling, and every so often a change, picked by four timers in [activities.toml](activities.toml).

```text
 TIER          COMES ROUND EVERY     IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 regular       2 to 5 minutes        about 155
 occasional    12 to 25 minutes      about 30
 rare          30 to 60 minutes      about 13
 super rare    3 to 6 hours          about 2 (never more than 3)
 chained       when another one      about 20 follow-ups, on top
               says so               of those
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 typical = the median of 200 simulated runs, as the schedule's own
 header puts it. she is busy about a third of the time and idling the
 rest. every activity starts on the next bar (3 s). the default run is
 10:00:00 with seed 1992
```

When a timer goes off, it picks an activity from its tier that is free to happen right now. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea can be busy while she is: a ship can sail past while she is dealing with a coconut, and it even waits for her to get busy first. `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a ten-hour run.

</details>

<p align="center">
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube. A young woman sits on a tiny island with one tall palm, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every few minutes, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is more headphones. A shark in headphones surfaces and nods to the same beat. Then everybody goes back to nodding.<br>
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime. 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps. Always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <b>The schedule:</b> more than 90 activities. Four timers pick them, from everyday routines every 2 to 5 minutes to super-rare callbacks every 3 to 6 hours, and some gags set off a follow-up of their own. Each one waits for the next bar of the music, so every gag lands on the beat.<br>
  <b>The sound:</b> every note, wave and splash is synthesized from code in <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><code>tools/make_audio.py</code></a>. No samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then export a frame-exact, YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm.<br>
  Assembly not required. Waiting is.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/65-memphis_opus_5.5-catalogo.svg" width="100%" alt="A page from an imaginary design catalogue, CATALOGO 1992, stamped GRUPPO ISOLOTTO: eight cards, each a flat colour panel with one big shape behind one object, a number tab, an Italian name and two lines in English. 01 BOTTIGLIA, a green bottle with a note and an arrow looping back: a message, it washes straight back. 02 PACCO, a drone carrying a parcel with headphones on it: by drone, contains more headphones. 03 TARTARUGA, a turtle with a zigzag shell: visits, stays a bit, says nothing. 04 GATTO, a grey tabby with a white chest napping on a floating crate: arrives on a crate, naps up the palm. 05 SQUALO, a shark fin in cream headphones with a music note: wears headphones, nods on the beat. 06 COCCO, a coconut on crab legs: lands on a crab, walks off with it. 07 SEGNALE, a phone over a palm crown and one signal bar of four: one bar, only at the top of the palm. 08 CAFFÈ FREDDO, an iced coffee with a striped straw: walks off on the sea, comes back with one.">

The catalogue is a joke. The pieces are not: every one of them is a real activity in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml), picked by a timer, with synthesized sound effects of its own.

| N° | piece | what happens | in the schedule |
|:---:|:---|:---|:---|
| 01 | **Bottiglia** (bottle) | She sends a message in a bottle. It washes straight back. Much later, a different bottle brings a reply. | `message_in_bottle`, `bottle_reply` |
| 02 | **Pacco** (parcel) | A delivery drone drops a parcel. It contains another pair of headphones. | `delivery_drone` |
| 03 | **Tartaruga** (turtle) | A sea turtle swims in, crawls up beside her, and they both doze off. | `turtle_visit` |
| 04 | **Gatto** (cat) | A grey tabby with a white chest arrives on a crate, climbs the palm and naps. One day it floats away again. It comes back another time. | `cat_visit` |
| 05 | **Squalo** (shark) | A fin circles the island. The shark surfaces in headphones and nods to the same beat. They nod. It leaves. | `shark_nod` |
| 06 | **Cocco** (coconut) | A coconut falls on a passing hermit crab. Then the coconut walks off. | `coconut_crab` |
| 07 | **Segnale** (signal) | One bar of signal, available only at the top of the palm. | `signal_hunt` |
| 08 | **Caffè freddo** (iced coffee) | She could leave any time. She walks out over the water, and comes back with an iced coffee. Never explained. | `leave_any_time` |

Also in the range, uncatalogued: a tour boat of selfie-takers, a bro on an electric hydrofoil who waves a shaka and carves off, bushcraft (fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing), a kumara she plants that grows over the course of the video, coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, and a sandcastle that the tide takes.

The banner keeps the same time: its master loop is the theme's 20 bars of 3 seconds, the counter steps once a bar, the letters hop once a bar, and she and the shark nod once a beat (0.75 s at 80 BPM). Counts are as of 2026-10-01; more activities arrive every few hours.

<details>
<summary><b>CREDITI</b>: credits, and what is made up</summary>
<br>

- **The look** is after the Memphis Group (Milan, 1980 to 1987) and the squiggles-and-confetti graphics it sent through late-80s pop culture. Credited as a reference only: the squiggle laminate, the shapes and the lettering here are drawn from scratch by a seeded generator, and no real print, piece of furniture or typeface is copied.
- **The idea** is an unofficial homage to *Johnny Castaway* (1992), which belongs to its owners. Nothing from it is used on this page.
- **Invented for this page:** Gruppo Isolotto (the "islet group", the design collective that supposedly made the island) and its Catalogo 1992. Neither exists, which is the least surprising fact on this page.
- **The Italian** is real and literal: *isolotto* is a small island, *catalogo* a catalogue, *scheda tecnica* a spec sheet, *crediti* credits; the pieces are bottle, parcel, turtle, cat, shark, coconut, signal and iced coffee.
- **Every sound** in the video is synthesized from code. **Every picture** here is original vector art from a seeded generator, so it comes out the same, byte for byte, every time. The schedule plays the same trick: seed 1992 gives the same ten hours, event for event.

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>open all day</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; ほぼ無人島 <i>(an almost uninhabited island)</i> &nbsp;·&nbsp; pop. 1<br>
  <sub>It is noon. It is always noon. The alley is just very narrow.</sub>
</p>

**Castaway** (working title) is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube in the spirit of the long lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. Mostly she idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often something happens. Then nothing happens again, at length, on purpose. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal scene: 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps, and always daytime.

The somethings: a message in a bottle that washes straight back to her feet, a delivery drone whose parcel is another pair of headphones, a sea turtle who drops by, a stray cat that arrives on a crate and naps up the palm, a shark in headphones who nods to the beat, and a coconut that lands on a hermit crab and then walks off with the crab inside. Once in a long while she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee, which is where the amber sign up there comes in. More than 90 activities wait in [activities.toml](activities.toml), most of them on four timers; each one starts on the next bar of the music, and every sound is synthesized from code.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

```text
├────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┬─────────────┤

│    │                          │ the phone just so              │             │

│    │                          │ feet. A reply comes later      │ + follow-up │
│ 4F │ SEA TURTLE, VISITING     │ in no hurry whatsoever         │ occasional  │

├────┴──────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┴─────────────┤

│         occasional  every 12 to 25 min    about 30 a run                     │

```

A selection of tenants, not the whole building: [activities.toml](activities.toml) held 94 activities on 2026-10-02, 81 of them on the four timers and 13 chained follow-ups that only ever start after something else (the bottle's reply, the kumara coming into leaf), and other sessions add more every few hours. The counts per run are medians of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, as the file's own header says, and the billboard's timer bars are drawn to that scale, which is why the super rare bar is a dot. Also in residence: jogging laps, fishing, coconut sipping, a sandcastle the tide takes, waving for rescue, and bushcraft (fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing).

When a timer goes off it picks one activity by weight from those free to run right now. Lanes let things overlap, so a visitor can come and go while she is busy with a coconut, and she is busy about a third of the time. The rest is idling, which is the main attraction. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992. `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a run; `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display, using the older Python reference renderer.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>WHAT THE SIGNS SAY</b>: the Japanese, translated</summary>

<br>

| Sign | Reads | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ほぼ無人島 | hobo mujintō | An almost uninhabited island. 無人島 is the everyday word for a desert island; ほぼ means "almost". Population: one, plus a cat on some days. |
| アイスコーヒー | aisu kōhī | Iced coffee, as written on café signs all over Japan. Set vertically, so each long-vowel mark ー stands upright, the way it does in vertical text. |
| open all day | | Shop hours, and also a project rule: it is always daytime, with no night scenes. |
| NOW SERVING 001 | | There has only ever been one customer. |

Every kanji and kana is a tube path drawn stroke by stroke for this banner and checked against the standard forms. They are there because they mean something about the island, not as decoration.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>MAINTENANCE LOG</b>: the tube that will not stay lit, and why it is not night</summary>

```text
  SALTGLASS NEON · SERVICE RECORD · UNIT CW-01 (CASTAWAY, 14 TUBES)

  TUBE 8 ...... crossbar, second A. On, off, on, long on, every 6.75 s.
                Reported. Maintenance has been notified.
                Maintenance is idling. On the beat.
  OTHER 13 .... steady. A slight hum, each sign on its own slow cycle.
  RAIN ........ a sun shower. The island's own rain shower is on the
                scene-life list as planned; the alley got one early.
  LIGHTING .... noon. Always noon. Daylight reaches the far end of the
                alley and stops there, out of politeness.
  CAM 1 ....... fixed shot. Has not panned since it was installed.
                Neither has the video.
  CUSTOMERS ... 1
```

The project has a rule that it is always daytime, and cyberpunk signage has a habit of night, so the banner splits the difference: it is midday, in an alley so narrow and so stacked with signs that the sun never gets in. At the far end the alley opens on the sea, and the sea is as bright as it ever is. The island is out there. She is on it, unless she has gone for a coffee.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>LINER NOTES</b>: every sound, made from code</summary>

<br>

Every sound in Castaway is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far, and the count keeps climbing.

- **The theme**: a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, on electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The crackle is synthesized too.
- **The ocean**: a seamless 60-second loop of its own.
- **Mastering**: the mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels can be set for the master and for each routine.
- **Reviews**: none. Nobody has listened to it yet. The sign went up before the shop opened, which is traditional.

The banner keeps the same time: the billboard cuts to a new frame every three bars, the shark nods once a beat, the waveform slides one period per bar, she walks two steps to the beat, and the whole story comes round every nine bars.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THE SIGNS ARE BENT</b>: the banner, taken apart</summary>

<br>

One SVG of about 125 KB, written by a dependency-free Node script that lives with the header gallery (`src/66-neon-signage_opus_5.5.mjs` there, not in this repo). It reads no clock and uses only seeded pseudo-random numbers, so it writes the same bytes every run.

- **Tubes.** Every lit letter is one centreline path drawn four times: a wide blurred halo with a fainter bloom around it, the coloured tube, a pale inner tube and a thin white core. The capitals are lines and arcs bent the way tubes bend, the lowercase is circles and stems, and the panel underneath carries each tube's shadow and a pair of standoffs per letter, so the glass stands off the board.
- **Kanji and kana.** Stroke paths on a 10 by 10 grid, one path per tube piece, set top to bottom.
- **The far end.** Sky, clouds, the sea, the island, one palm, a raft, glints that twinkle in turn, and her, clipped to the gap between the buildings so she can walk round the corner and out of sight.
- **The street.** Everything above, mirrored about the quay, squashed and smeared downward by a vertical-only blur, then cut into streaks by two sets of ripples drifting apart. The bad tube's reflection flickers with it. Rain is two sheets of thin lines, each sliding exactly one tile per cycle, with splashes opening on the ground.
- **Type.** No text elements and no fonts: the labels are a stroke font on a 4 by 6 grid, the LED display is a 5 by 7 dot font drawn as round-capped dots.
- **Calm mode.** With reduced motion set, everything holds one complete frame: every tube lit, the shark on the billboard, her on the island.

</details>

<p align="center"><sub>Unofficial: inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), and not affiliated with it or its owners. Cyberpunk neon signage is a style reference only: no real sign, film, game, brand or typeface is reproduced, and all art here is original. Saltglass Neon and Noon Alley are made up. The rain is a sun shower.</sub></p>

<br>

<details>
<summary><b>Program: CASTAWAY</b>: the tape, block by block</summary>

```text
 CASTAWAY                                          side A   counter 000
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  #  BLOCK                WHAT IS ON IT
  1  Program: CASTAWAY    the loader: python tools/serve.py, a web page
                          at http://127.0.0.1:8765/ with a live preview
                          and an export to MP4 (frame-exact, in the
                          browser; the server mixes in the sound)
  2  Bytes:   SCREEN$     6912 bytes: 6144 of picture, 768 of colour.
                          the island above. two colours per 8x8 cell
  3  Bytes:   SCHEDULE    activities.toml: more than 90 activities and
                          four timers, checked by python tools/schedule.py
  4  Bytes:   THEME       60 seconds, 80 BPM, F major, loops forever
  5  Bytes:   SFX         more than 150 sounds, none of them recorded
  6  Bytes:   VIDEO       10:00:00 at 24 fps: 864,000 frames
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  duplicated by Leader Tone Duplicating. rewind fully before returning
```

At roughly 170 bytes a second, block 6 would bring in one 6912-byte frame every 41 seconds or so, and the whole video in a little over 13 months, as long as nobody touches the volume knob. The browser export manages 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p, so at that rate the same ten hours would take a bit over three. We consider that unsporting.

To run it the old way: <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>Symbol Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>, <kbd>Symbol Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>, <kbd>Enter</kbd>, then press play on the tape. To run it the new way: `python tools/serve.py`.

<sub>Leader Tone Duplicating is made up. So is the tape.</sub>

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SCHEDULE</b>: four timers and a great deal of calm</summary>

Everything she does lives in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml): more than 90 activities (94 on 2 October 2026, and the list grows every few hours), each on one of four timers or chained after another one.

```text
 TIMER         COMES ROUND EVERY     IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
 regular       2 to 5 minutes        about 155
 occasional    12 to 25 minutes      about 30
 rare          30 to 60 minutes      about 13
 super rare    3 to 6 hours          about 2  (never more than 3)
 chained       only after another    the tide after a sandcastle
```

"Typical" is the median of 200 simulated runs. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and every activity starts on the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), which is why the screen above loops every 8 bars. The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`; `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates one.

A short tour of the gags: the message in a bottle that washes straight back (a different bottle brings a reply, later); the delivery drone whose parcel is another pair of headphones; the sea turtle who visits; the grey tabby who arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats off again; the hunt for signal (one bar, top of the palm); the shark in headphones who nods to the beat; the tour boat of selfie-takers; the bro on an electric hydrofoil who throws a shaka and carves off; the kumara she plants, which grows over the video; and the very rare day she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. She could leave any time.

Around her, 26 bits of scene life: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; birds, planes with vapour trails, whales, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SOUND</b>: made by code, heard by nobody (yet)</summary>

Every sound comes out of [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.

```text
 THEME     60-second seamless loop, 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi
           20 bars of exactly 3 seconds
           electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
 OCEAN     60-second seamless loop
 MIX       -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP
 LEVELS    a master for each kind of sound, and one per routine
```

Nobody has listened to any of it yet, so we will not tell you it sounds lovely. The meters are happy, though.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THIS SCREEN LOADS</b>: the rules it keeps</summary>

The banner is one SVG, drawn by a small Node script with no packages, and it keeps the rules of an early-80s 8-bit home computer, because the rules are the look:

- **256 by 192 pixels, cut into 32 by 24 cells, two colours per cell.** One INK, one PAPER and one BRIGHT bit for the pair. Where the palm meets the sea the frond tips go a darker green, because the cell they share with the water is not BRIGHT. That is not shading. That is the rules.
- **The picture loads in memory order.** Three thirds, top to bottom; inside each third, the top pixel line of all eight text rows, then the second line, and so on, so it fills like a venetian blind. The colour comes last, one row of cells at a time.
- **The border is the tape.** Thick red and cyan bands for the pilot tone, thin blue and yellow stripes for data, where a 1 bit is twice as thick as a 0 bit. The stripes here are the real bits of the word CASTAWAY.
- **It waits for the bar.** The loop is 24 seconds, which is 8 bars of the theme at 80 BPM, and every phase starts on a bar line. Once loaded, her head, the shark and the music note keep the beat (0.75 seconds), and the bottom lines change every bar.

The font, the logo letters and the island are drawn from scratch in the generator; nothing is lifted from a real machine or a real game. With reduced motion on, it skips the loading and shows the finished screen. The stripes are slowed right down and only roll while it loads.

</details>

<br>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Insert disk. Then wait. That is most of the video.</b><br>
  A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose. Even the boot screen is waiting.
</p>

**Castaway** *(working title)* is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers more headphones. A shark in headphones nods along. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, who walks off wearing it. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted in a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime look: 16:9, 1080p, and always daytime.

There are more than 90 activities, most of them on four timers that go off anywhere from every few minutes to once every few hours, and each one waits for the next bar of the music before it starts, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code: no samples, no recordings.

To boot it, from the project root:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4. Castaway is in development and no video has been published yet, so for now the only way to watch her wait is to run it.

<details>
<summary><b>PLEASE INSERT DISK 2</b>: the schedule, and everything that turns up</summary>

<br>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) holds more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-02: 81 on four timers and 13 chained follow-ups), and more turn up every few hours.

| Timer | Comes round every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| Occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| Rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| Super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 a run | about 2 |
| Chained | never on a timer: only after something else | about 20 |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs, as the top of the file says. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so the sea carries on while she is busy with a coconut: a ship can sail past behind her, and it even waits for her to get busy first. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, and a bar is 3 seconds long. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992.

What turns up, now and then:

- a message in a bottle, which washes straight back; a different bottle brings a reply, later
- a delivery drone, whose parcel is another pair of headphones
- a sea turtle, who visits
- a grey tabby with a white chest, who arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again (and comes back another time)
- the signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the very top of the palm
- a shark wearing headphones, who nods to the beat
- a tour boat full of selfie-takers
- a coconut that falls on a hermit crab, after which the coconut walks off with the crab wearing it
- a bro on an electric hydrofoil, who waves with a shaka and carves off
- "she could leave any time": she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee
- bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing
- a kumara she plants, which grows over the course of the video
- and in between: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle the tide takes, and waving for rescue, just in case

The scene keeps itself busy too: 26 entries, 4 always-on effects and 22 timed events. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.


<details>
<summary><b>ISLAND MEDITATION</b>: the red box, explained, so nobody files a bug</summary>

<br>

On the machines this banner borrows from, a black box with a flashing red frame at the top of the screen meant something had gone badly wrong, and its name came from an in-house joke about sitting very still on a balance board. Castaway's box means the opposite. Nothing has gone wrong. She has just been sitting very still, and the machine cannot tell the difference.

```text
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                      │
 │   Nothing has failed.   Nothing has happened.   That is the video.   │
 │                 Island Meditation #00001992.00036000                 │
 │                                                                      │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- `00001992` is the default seed.
- `00036000` is the default run in seconds: 10:00:00.
- Both are in plain decimal. The real thing used hex, but nobody here is in a hurry.
- The frame flashes with the music: on for one beat, off for the next, which is two thirds of a flash a second.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>DISK 1 OF 1</b>: how the banner is made, credits and greetz</summary>

<br>

The banner is drawn on a model of the real screen: 640 pixels across and 200 lines down, every pixel twice as tall as it is wide, which is why the text comes out stretched the way it did on a television. Every shape is filled and outlined on that pixel grid, so each edge is a true one-pixel line, and each scene keeps to its own small palette: white, black, grey and two periwinkles for the card (plus one coral hair tie), blue, white, near-black and orange for the desktop and everything in its window, island included, and red on black for the alert.

- **One loop, 42 seconds:** 14 bars at 80 BPM. Every change is a hard cut or a step, and the big ones land on the beat. The card holds for the first five seconds, so the name is there on the first frame.
- **Her:** she nods on every beat, and so does the shark when it turns up, which is the only rehearsal they have had.
- **Calm:** no large area flashes. The alert frame is a thin border at two thirds of a flash a second. With reduced motion switched on, the banner holds on the insert-disk card.
- **Size:** about 120 KB, with no fonts and nothing external. Both faces (the 8x8 screen font and the slanted title capitals) are original bitmaps in the generator.

It is regenerated by a standalone Node script with no packages. No real system's name, logo, font or drawing was copied: the hand, the disk, the desktop and both fonts are new, and the alert's wording is a parody, not a quote.

```text
 DISK 1 OF 1 .......... Castaway. Label upside down, as is traditional
 DUPLICATED BY ........ Backwash Duplicating. One copy, sent by bottle.
                        It came straight back
 BOOT ROM ............. Sandstart 1.0. Starts on sand
 DESKTOP .............. Shorebench 1.0. 36000 free seconds
 RAFT DISK ............ holds one raft
 TIDE ................. the bin. Whatever goes in, the tide takes
 INSPIRED BY .......... Johnny Castaway (1992), the island screensaver.
                        Unofficial, and not affiliated with its owners

 GREETZ
 the Sit Still Society ......... ten hours, a new personal best
 the Watched Pot Club .......... the kettle is on. It has been on a while
 everyone who leaves this tab open, nodding along
```

</details>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, filed under <code>C:\ISLAND</code>. Most of the files are waiting.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often, always on the next bar of the music, something happens. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.

Up there, the island is a directory. `ship.pas` is a ship that passes. `crab.hat` is a coconut that lands on a hermit crab, who keeps it. `drone.arj` is a parcel by drone with one file inside: more headphones. `PALM\TOP\signal.bar` is one bar of signal, found at the very top of the palm and nowhere else. Press F6 on `bottle.msg` and it moves to `C:\ISLAND\SEA`. Then it washes straight back. More than 90 activities wait their turn, most of them on four timers from **regular** (every 2 to 5 minutes) to **super rare** (every 3 to 6 hours), the rest chained on as follow-ups. Every sound in it is synthesized from code: no samples, no recordings, no borrowed loops.

```sh
python tools/serve.py        # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>F3 View</b>: how to read the screen up there</summary>

<br>

- **The left panel is the island.** Every file in `C:\ISLAND` is an activity from [`activities.toml`](activities.toml), apart from `her.nod`, which is what she does in between: *Lasts* is its real duration range and *Tier* is the timer that picks it. The status line under the list gives the activity's own id, so `ship.pas` is `ship_passes_unseen` and `crab.hat` is `coconut_crab`.
- **The cursor is her.** She has one lane and does one thing at a time. A file that turns yellow is running in a lane of its own while she is busy with something else. In the banner that is `ship.pas`, in lane `sea_sky`, which the schedule deliberately starts while she has her hands full: it will wait up to ten minutes for her to be busy with a coconut, a sandcastle, a fishing line or a jogging lap.
- **The right panel is a Quick View** of the file under the cursor, drawn in half-block pixels in the 16 text colours. One palette register is redefined to a skin tone, as VGA allowed. The caption underneath says what is happening, in case the pixels do not.
- **The counter in the top-right corner**, where a clock would sit, counts the bars of the theme: 20 bars of 3 seconds. One loop of the banner is one loop of the theme, 60 seconds.
- **Everything moves in whole steps, on hard cuts.** The cursor goes a row at a time and the pictures a half-block pixel at a time, with nothing in between. That is the house style of the twin-panel commander, and it happens to be the project's own rule too: hard cuts and stepped movement are its motion defaults.
- **The 8.3 names.** `her.nod` lasts *the rest*, in tier *between*. `sandcast.le` has lost the end of its name to the 8.3 rule, which is roughly what the tide does to it. `leave.any` is the super rare one: she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. `kumara.grw` is a chained follow-up: hours after she plants the kumara, it quietly comes into leaf. The two coconuts in `PALM` are not activities at all: they are hanging, and their tier is gravity.

</details>

## 70 · Handheld Boot Logo

<sub><code>70-handheld-boot-logo_opus_5.5.md</code></sub>

<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  Shown here on a handheld with four shades of green, which the sea, the sand, the palm and she all have to share.
</p>

One young woman in cream headphones, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens: a message in a bottle washes straight back, a drone delivers a parcel that turns out to be another pair of headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it. Once in a very long while she remembers she could leave any time, walks out over the water, and comes back with an iced coffee. The attract mode on that little screen reports this as it happens. It is not exaggerating.

<p align="center">
  <sub>Working title. An unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime for YouTube: 16:9, 1080p at 24 fps, always daytime.</sub>
</p>

</p>

```sh
# live preview and MP4 export
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

No cartridge, no build step: the renderer is [a web page](web/index.html) of plain ES modules that previews live and exports frame-exact H.264 in the browser, and the server mixes in the sound and writes the MP4. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings. Nothing is published yet, and nobody has heard the soundtrack, including the code that wrote it.

Between those: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle the tide takes, waving for rescue, a sea turtle who visits, and bushcraft (fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing). The scene keeps itself busy too: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built, and birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned, 26 entries in all.

<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A 10-hour lo-fi island video. Almost nothing happens. That is the game.</b><br>
  One young woman in cream headphones, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of very calm waiting.
  She idles and nods to the music. Every so often something happens, always on the next bar of the music,
  so every gag lands on the beat. Nobody scores.<br>
  <sub>Working title, in development: no video is published yet. A stationary-frame video for YouTube, 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps, always daytime. An unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners.</sub>

**PUSH START.** No cartridge, no build step, no npm: just Python and a browser.

```sh
python tools/serve.py     # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py  # validate the schedule and simulate a 10-hour run
```

The page plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4: Chrome encodes the video frame-exact with WebCodecs (H.264; 1080p exports have run at 68 to 78 frames a second), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two. Every sound is synthesized from code: no samples, no ready-made loops, no recordings.

<details>
<summary><b>INSTRUCTION BOOKLET</b>: controls, object of the game, characters</summary>
<br>

```text
 CONTROLS ..................................................... NONE
   SHE PLAYS HERSELF. YOU MAY ADJUST THE SOUND LEVELS, IN MASTER
   AND PER ROUTINE. THAT IS THE WHOLE CONTROLLER.

 OBJECT OF THE GAME ........................................... WAIT
   SHE IDLES FOR ABOUT TWO THIRDS OF A RUN AND IS BUSY FOR THE REST.
   A RUN IS 10:00:00. SEED 1992. SAME SEED, SAME SCHEDULE, EVERY TIME.

 SCORING ...................................................... NONE
   HI-SCORE 000000. IT HAS NEVER BEEN BEATEN, OR ATTEMPTED.

 NIGHT LEVELS ................................................. NONE
   IT IS ALWAYS DAYTIME. HOUSE RULE.
```

**Characters you may meet** (most of them, eventually):

- **The castaway.** Brown hair in a loose low bun, cream headphones, coral tank top, cream shorts, bare feet. Nods on the beat.
- **The hermit crab.** Gets a coconut dropped on it, then walks off wearing it.
- **The stray grey tabby** with the white chest. Arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. Comes back another time.
- **The sea turtle.** Visits.
- **The shark in headphones.** Nods to the same beat as her. See SOUND TEST.
- **The bro on the electric hydrofoil.** Waves a shaka and carves off.
- **The tour boat of selfie-takers.** Takes photos. Leaves.

**Items:** a message in a bottle that washes straight back to her feet (a different bottle brings a reply, later); a delivery drone's parcel, which is another pair of headphones; one bar of signal, found at the top of the palm; an iced coffee, fetched by walking out over the water and back, because she could leave any time; a kumara, planted, which grows over the course of the video; a sandcastle, until the tide takes it.

**Bonus stages:** bushcraft. Fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SCHEDULE</b>: more than 90 activities, four timers, one beat</summary>
<br>

Everything she can do lives in [activities.toml](activities.toml): more than 90 activities, most on four timers, the rest chained after another gag. Each timer keeps its own clock. Typical counts below are the median of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, as the file's own header gives them:

```text
TIMER         COMES ROUND EVERY     IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
REGULAR       2 TO 5 MINUTES        ABOUT 155
OCCASIONAL    12 TO 25 MINUTES      ABOUT 30
RARE          30 TO 60 MINUTES      ABOUT 13
SUPER RARE    3 TO 6 HOURS          ABOUT 2 (AT MOST 3 A RUN)
CHAINED       AFTER ANOTHER GAG     ABOUT 20 FOLLOW-UPS
```

Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut. The ship waits until she is busy. It is that kind of ship. Around her the scene keeps itself busy: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are on the way.

`python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a run. `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display (the older Python reference renderer; [web/index.html](web/index.html) is the renderer now). The project log is [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

Every sound is made by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no ready-made loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. There are more than 150 sound files and counting. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii, V, I, vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP.

Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The shark is nodding anyway. The shark is a drawing.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>TECHNICAL NOTES</b>: how the title screen obeys the console</summary>
<br>

The banner is drawn the way an 8-bit console would have to draw it, and the generator refuses to write it otherwise:

- **One screen is 256 by 240 pixels, built from 8 by 8 tiles.** Wave marks and horizon glare are repeating tiles rather than scattered pixels, so the title screen needs 245 unique tiles and the demo screen 251, inside the 256 one pattern table holds. The right-hand panel shows the counts.
- **Colour comes in 16 by 16 zones.** Each zone picks one of four background palettes of three colours, plus one backdrop colour shared by all. The generator gives every zone its palette and stops with an error if any zone needs a colour its palette cannot show; the zone map in the right-hand panel is that result. It is why the T of the logo is a palm: the T's two zone columns use the palm's palette, and every other letter is sand above the zone line and gold below it.
- **Sprites:** four palettes of three colours, eight sprites to a scanline at most. The timeline is sampled 30 times a second to check; the busiest line carries four.
- **The palette is decoded, not copied.** No emulator's colour table is used: the 64 colours are computed from the composite signal levels published on the NESdev wiki, the way an emulator computes its own. Like every such palette, it is one decoder's opinion of a signal nobody ever specified a monitor for.
- **One palette entry cycles.** Background palette 0, colour 3, steps white, pale cyan, cyan, pale cyan: the logo's highlights and the island's foam shimmer together without a single pixel moving. The swatch in the left-hand panel, and its number, step along with it.
- **It keeps the theme's time.** 80 BPM, a beat every 0.75 seconds, a bar every 3. The banner loops every 30 seconds, ten bars: title, a hard cut to the demo at 15, a hard cut back at 27 with the logo dropping in, and the loop lands on its opening frame. Hard cuts and stepped movement, which also happen to be the video's own motion defaults. With reduced motion requested, it holds still on the title.

</details>

</p>

<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  <sub>Working title. In development. An unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="tools/serve.py"><b>run it</b></a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="activities.toml">the schedule</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="tools/make_audio.py">the sound</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="MUSING.md">the notes</a>
</p>

One tiny island, one tall palm, one raft, one young woman in cream headphones, and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A shark in headphones nods along. A coconut falls on a hermit crab, and the crab leaves wearing it. It is a stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, sunny hand-painted coastal anime, and always daytime.

The screen up there keeps score the arcade way. Gags are points. Headphones are lives, and the drone is the extra life. There is no joystick, because there is nothing to do: in a typical ten-hour run she is busy about a third of the time and idle for the rest, and the idle is the point.

More than 90 activities live in [activities.toml](activities.toml). Most of them run on four timers: something regular every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, and super rare every 3 to 6 hours; the rest are follow-ups that another gag sets off. Lanes let them overlap, and every one waits for the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), so the punchlines land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, mixed to -14 LUFS. Nobody has listened to it yet. It is extremely well measured.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

Live preview in the page, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 with WebCodecs, and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) checks the schedule and simulates a ten-hour run; [`python tools/render_demo.py --dev`](tools/render_demo.py) renders a dev reel of every activity. Nothing is published yet, so for now the only way to watch her do nothing for ten hours is to run it yourself.

<details>
<summary><b>XY MODE</b>: the theme, drawn as one green line</summary>
<br>
<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/72-vector-beam-display_opus_5.5-scope.svg" width="100%" alt="An oscilloscope screen with a green graticule. One closed green trace draws the theme's four chords, one bar each, as Lissajous figures that drift and then morph on the bar line: Gm9 and Dm9 as 6:5, root against minor third; C13 and Fmaj9 as 5:4, root against major third. Beside it, a sand-coloured now-playing readout: NOW PLAYING, THE THEME, 60 S LOOP. 80 BPM, F MAJOR, 20 BARS OF 3 S, II-V-I-VI. Four chord boxes, Gm9, C13, Fmaj9 and Dm9, the current one lit. X: ROOT, Y: the current third and its ratio. E-PIANO, KALIMBA, SOFT DRUMS, VINYL CRACKLE. EVERY SOUND SYNTHESIZED FROM CODE. NO SAMPLES. In dim letters: DRAWN FROM THE CHORD NAMES, NOT FROM THE FILE. LISTENERS TO DATE: 0.">
</p>

On an XY scope the left channel moves the beam sideways and the right channel moves it up and down, so a sound draws its own picture. A silent README cannot do that honestly, so this one fakes it in the open: the four chords are the ones [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py) plays, one per 3-second bar (Gm9, C13, Fmaj9, Dm9, a ii-V-I-vi in F), and each is drawn as its root against its third, rounded to the nearest small ratio so the figure closes. The real file sounds like whatever it sounds like. Nobody knows yet.

</details>

```text
 │  BANK  TIMER         COMES ROUND EVERY   PER 10-HOUR RUN   1 2 3 4 5 6  │
```

Counts are the median of 200 simulated ten-hour runs, as the file's own header says. The chained bank is the follow-ups: the tide that comes for the sandcastle, and the like. Rebalancing the timers is on the list for later; for now the occasional bank is crowded and some of its gags wait a long time for their turn.

<details>
<summary><b>ATTRACT MODE</b>: the banner's minute, bar by bar</summary>

```text
 BAR  TIME   STATUS LINE                   WHAT THE BEAM DRAWS
 ───  ─────  ────────────────────────────  ────────────────────────────────
 01   00:00  ALL QUIET ON THE ISLAND       the title, redrawn stroke by
                                           stroke; a plane crosses
 03   00:06  BOTTLE AWAY                   she throws; it lands; it drifts
 05   00:12  BOTTLE BACK. STILL HERS       it washes straight back to her
 08   00:21  ALL QUIET                     nodding, on every beat

                                           floats off with the tide

```

The real video spaces these out by minutes or hours. The banner crams an unusually eventful afternoon into one minute, which is also the length of the theme, so the whole screen loops when the music would.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SERVICE MANUAL</b>: how the screen is drawn</summary>

**No pixels.** The banner is one SVG, made by a Node script with no dependencies. Every line is a stroke drawn three times, a wide faint halo, a mid glow and a thin near-white core, so it glows without a blur filter. The lettering is an original stroke alphabet (a few straight segments per letter, chamfered corners), drawn as paths so it looks the same for every viewer.

**The overlay.** The beam is white. The colour comes from three tinted rectangles laid over the tube with a multiply blend, the way a plastic overlay sheet works: coral over the title strip, aqua over the island, sand over the status line. Anything that crosses a boundary changes colour there; the headphones do, on their way up to the lives counter.

**The island.** A 3D wireframe (sand contours, the palm with bark rings and drooping fronds, two rocks, some bushes, a five-log raft) on a slow turntable, 26 degrees each way, once a minute. It is projected at 16 keyframes and played back as one path morph with eased timing, so the sway has no corners. She, the parcel and the crab are flat cut-outs that ride the same turntable. The real video never moves its camera, so somebody had to.

**The sea.** Fifteen broken swell lines roll towards you, one arriving per bar. Each line's shape depends only on how far away it is, so the loop has no seam.

**The title.** Its ghost is always on screen, so the name reads from the first frame. At the top of every minute the beam redraws the front face stroke by stroke, with a spark where each stroke ends, holds it with a faint shimmer, and lets it fade back to the ghost in the order it was drawn. Twice a minute the whole tube dims for an instant, the way a busy vector screen flickers.

**Reduced motion.** With reduced motion switched on, the screen holds still on a complete first frame: title lit, island at rest, status reading ALL QUIET ON THE ISLAND.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>GREETINGS FROM THE BEAM</b></summary>
<br>

To the island regulars: the sea turtle, who visits; the stray cat (grey tabby, white chest), who arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats off again, and then comes back; the bro on the electric hydrofoil (shaka received); the tour boat of selfie-takers; the shark, for wearing headphones correctly; the hermit crab, for wearing a coconut with dignity; the kumara, growing as fast as it can; and the ship, which as usual waited until she was busy.

To the vector arcade cabinets and home vector consoles of 1979 to 1984, and to the people who make music that draws pictures on oscilloscopes: credited here as the inspiration for the look. Nothing of theirs is copied; the alphabet, the island and the overlay are all drawn from scratch. SLOWBEAM is made up, like the score.

</details>

<br>

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of island, tuned to 80 BPM. Signal: one bar, top of the palm.</b>
</p>

<p align="center">
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the 10-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often something happens. Mostly, it does not. That is the point.<br>
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p, and always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  More than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-02) wait in <a href="activities.toml"><code>activities.toml</code></a>, most of them on four timers, from <i>regular</i> (every 2 to 5 minutes) to <i>super rare</i> (every 3 to 6 hours), and each one starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat: a bottle that washes straight back, a drone that delivers another pair of headphones, a shark in headphones nodding along. Every sound is synthesized from code in <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><code>tools/make_audio.py</code></a>: no samples, no ready-made loops, no recordings.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then one button for a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. In development: no video is out yet.<br>
  The banner is the display in shop <b>DEMO</b> mode, which packs a few hours of gags into sixty seconds. The real thing spreads them over ten hours and leaves the <b>IDLE</b> lamp on in between.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>LAMP TEST</b>: what every light on the panel means</summary>

```text
 IDLETRONIC IR-600 · DISPLAY LEGEND
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 LAMP         MEANS                                        LIT
 DEMO         shop demo: a few hours of gags in 60 s       blinking
 PLAY         the video is playing                         always
 REPEAT 1     the theme is a seamless 60 s loop            always
 ♪            the beat: 80 BPM, one every 0.75 s           on the beat
 ST           stereo                                       always
 IDLE         she idles, nodding to the music              most of it
 BUSY         she is doing something                       about 1/3
 DAYTIME      it is daytime                                always
 NIGHT        it is night                                  never
 SYNTH        every sound is synthesized from code         always
 SAMPLES      a sound came from a recording                never
 TIME 0:00    time into the 60 s theme loop                counting
 TUNED 80.0   tempo, in BPM (F major, ii-V-I-vi)           always

 OCCASIONAL   this gag came off the 12 to 25 min timer     per gag
 RARE         this gag came off the 30 to 60 min timer     per gag
 SUPER RARE   this gag came off the 3 to 6 h timer         not today
 LEVEL        drums, e.piano, kalimba: the theme's score   by the bar
              vinyl crackle, surf: L and R                 bouncing
 ISLAND       every gag is printed on the glass, faintly,  in turn
              and lights up when its timer comes round
```

The NIGHT lamp is not broken. The island is always daytime: that is a project rule, so the lamp is there for completeness and nothing else.

The drums, e.piano and kalimba meters are worked out from the theme's own score in [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py), in step with the BAR counter: keys only in bars 1 and 2, drums from bar 3, the kalimba from bar 7, and only kick and rim in bars 17 to 20 while the keys' filter closes. The meters have read the music. Nobody has heard it yet.

Every message lands exactly on a bar line, like the gags do: in the video, every activity waits for the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. The cat in bar 12 has its own lane too, so she stays IDLE; the shark in bar 11 needs her to nod back, so she is BUSY. That makes 8 busy bars out of 20. A real run is nearer a third. <details>
<summary><b>TROUBLESHOOTING</b>: before you call the island</summary>

- **The NIGHT lamp will not light.** Correct. It is always daytime on the island. That is a rule, not a fault.
- **The SAMPLES lamp will not light.** Correct. Every sound is generated by code. There is nothing to sample.
- **SUPER RARE never lights.** Leave the unit on. That timer goes off every 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 times a run, and the demo lasts one minute.
- **The display said BONK.** A coconut fell on a hermit crab. The crab is fine. The crab is wearing the coconut now.
- **The DRUMS meter goes quiet for the first six seconds.** Correct. The theme opens with two bars of keys only. The kalimba waits until bar 7. Everyone on this island waits for something.
- **It only ever says ONE BAR.** That is the signal. It is at the top of the palm. She has checked.
- **The buttons on the picture do nothing.** They are a picture. The working ones are in the web page: `python tools/serve.py`, then http://127.0.0.1:8765/.
- **There is no sound.** GitHub keeps sound out of READMEs. Nobody has heard the soundtrack yet anyway, including the code that wrote it.
- **Nothing is happening.** Correct. Wait for it.

<sub>The IDLETRONIC IR-600, its maker and its model number are invented for this README; no real receiver was opened. The panel is drawn by a script: 16-segment and 7-segment cells, an original stroke font, no fonts, no bitmaps. The island is original too.</sub>

</details>

<br>

<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi video of one tiny island, one tall palm and no signal whatsoever.</b><br>
  <sub>Unofficial and drawn from scratch: inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver. Not affiliated with it or its owners.</sub>
</p>

A young woman, a tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often something happens: her message in a bottle drifts straight back to her, a drone delivers a parcel that turns out to be more headphones, a shark in headphones nods along on the beat, and a coconut lands on a hermit crab, who walks off wearing it. That is her phone in the picture, face up on the sand. It says *No network*. It is right. There is one bar, at the very top of the palm.

Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, always daytime, 16:9 at 1080p, made for YouTube. **[More than 90 activities](activities.toml)** on four timers, from every few minutes to once every few hours, plus follow-ups that only ever happen after another one. Each starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <a href="tools/serve.py"><kbd>Call</kbd></a>&nbsp;
  <a href="activities.toml"><kbd>Calendar</kbd></a>&nbsp;
  <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><kbd>Tones</kbd></a>&nbsp;
  <a href="MUSING.md"><kbd>Notes</kbd></a>&nbsp;
  <kbd>Menu</kbd> <sub>(everything else is below)</sub>
</p>

The renderer is [a web page](web/index.html) with a live preview and an export button: frame-exact H.264 straight out of the browser, and the server mixes in the sound for a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. It is in development, so no video is out yet. The phone has been told.

--[ Introduction

Welcome to issue 0x01. Volume 0x00, because nothing is released yet.

<b>Castaway</b> is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube: one tiny island, one
tall palm, one raft, and a young woman in cream headphones with 0x8ca0
seconds to fill. She idles. She nods to the music. Every so often, on
the next bar, something happens: her bottle washes straight back, a
drone delivers more headphones, a coconut walks off worn by a hermit
crab. Then she goes back to nodding. That is the main attraction.

An unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver Johnny Castaway.
Sunny, hand-painted and always daytime, with more than 0x5a (90)
activities on four timers and every sound synthesized from code. Still
in development. The rest of this issue is paperwork.

    $ python <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a>        then open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a>
